title: Chilled ready meal tray sealer, leaking packs
tests: Process/quality failure: leaking seals; causes across equipment, materials, method, measurement. Deterioration must be not_applicable for non-wear causes.
summary: Sauce leaked from sealed trays of a chilled curry ready meal on Line 3. Seal check once per shift missed it. Film from a new supplier lot, a sealing temperature setpoint changed at a changeover, and sauce on the seal area all appear in the notes. Tree blames the sealing head only.

problem.title: Leaking seals on chilled curry trays, Line 3
problem.site: Chilled meals factory, Western Sydney NSW
problem.whatHappened: On 22 Apr 2026 the retail DC rejected a pallet of 400 g butter chicken trays after leaking packs were found. About 3% of a 2-hour production run was leaking at the seal. The seal check once per shift did not find it. Film from a new supplier lot was loaded that morning and the sealing temperature was changed at the changeover.
problem.where: Lidding film seal on the long edge of the tray, tray flange.
problem.when: Run started after the morning changeover to butter chicken; leaks found from about 09:00 to 11:00 production.
problem.impact: 1,440 trays on one pallet rejected, a further 3,600 trays held for 100% inspection, retailer complaint raised.
problem.makeModel: Inline tray sealer, 6 trays per stroke
problem.duty: Seals lidding film on 400 g curry trays

evidence.title: Leaking seal sample trays
evidence.note: Channel leaks at the long edge seal; sauce residue visible in the seal channel on 4 of 6 samples.

evidence.title: Sealer setpoint log
evidence.note: Temperature 175 C on the previous run; 185 C after the changeover. Dwell time unchanged, pressure not logged.

evidence.title: Film delivery and CoA
evidence.note: New lidding film lot from the new supplier, received 20 Apr. Certificate states seal initiation temperature range; incoming check not done.

evidence.title: Shift seal check record
evidence.note: One tray tested by dye test at 07:00 and passed. Next check due at 15:00.

evidence.title: Filler nozzle and tray flange
evidence.note: Filler dripping on 2 of 6 nozzles; sauce on flange of some trays before sealing.

problemDraft.roughNotes: ts03 leaking seals on butter chicken. dc rejected a pallet, about 3% of the 9-11am run leaking. we had a changeover that morning, seal temp went to 185 from 175 for the new film, i think. new film lot from the new supplier went on at the same time. sauce splash on the flange on some trays, filler was dripping. seal check is once a shift and passed at 7am. ncr 26-0231.

mustSuggest.idea: Sauce on the seal flange from filler drips contaminating the seal
New film lot from the new supplier with a different seal initiation range
Change control: a new film or supplier does not trigger seal parameter validation
Setpoints not locked or verified at changeover (temperature, dwell, pressure)
Seal check frequency of once per shift is too sparse to catch a run problem (measurement)
Operators had no recipe card or verified setpoint for the new film, as a system gap

acceptable: Sealing head wear or heater element drift
Ambient temperature of the chilled room
wrongOrDangerous: Marking any deterioration as forced for non-wear causes (setpoint, film, check frequency)
Claiming the analysis meets a food standard

mustFlag.note: Flagged root with no evidence linked
Only the sealer temperature branch: no materials, measurement, or filler drip

mustNotFlag: claim of HACCP or standard compliance
challenge.expectation: Should raise measurement (once-a-shift check) and supplier or material batch as the missing branches; summary in plain words.
deliberateWeaknesses: Branch only blames the operator (blame) and the machine; no materials (film lot, supplier), measurement (once-per-shift check) or filler drip angle
n1 and n2 no evidence although e2 exists
Root n2 is human with no system cause
a2 retrains for a system gap
Verification of the countermeasure absent (no leak test frequency)
No supplier or incoming check angle

capa.deteriorationReasoning: A setpoint, a film lot and a check frequency are not wear. Say so in the reason.
corrective: Hold and inspect affected pallets (a1 done)
Check and clean filler nozzles, tray flange clean-up

preventive.what: Setpoint card per film and product with temperature, dwell and pressure, verified by a second person at changeover
Lock or verify setpoints at changeover before the first pack leaves the line
In-process seal check by dye or vacuum leak test, increased in frequency after a changeover or film change
preventive.interval: first pack, then every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours, then hourly (starting point to review with QA)

preventive.what: Supplier approval and incoming check for lidding film including seal range test; change control for new lots or suppliers
Fix filler nozzle drips and add a drip tray or sensor
preventive.interval: next planned stop and weekly check

preventive.what: Training on the new setpoint card as part of the system change

capa.spares: Not forced for a process failure. Optionally hold a spare sealing head heater and temperature sensor, only if shown relevant.
capa.rollout: Other lines and products using the same lidding film or supplier; other changeovers where the film changes.
unacceptable: Retrain or remind operators as the only action
Claim the analysis meets HACCP or any standard
Forcing a spares or vibration monitoring action
Mark the film or setpoint as forced deterioration

hardChecks.processRules: No deterioration other than not_applicable on setting, method, material or check causes. No claim of HACCP/SQF/BRC compliance. No spares or vibration monitoring forced into CAPA.
